app.title: EukaSurvey — The Genomic Resource Explorer for Eukaryotes
app.summary: A person picks a root clade from a list of common ones or types any taxon ID, and sees where it sits in the tree of life along with a short encyclopedia blurb. Summary cards show how many species the clade holds and, for each of four kinds of public genomic data, how many species are covered, what share that is, and the total count. They then pick a rank to split the clade by, optionally require certain kinds of data, sort and cap the number of groups, and generate a tree with bar charts beside each group and a sortable table. The displayed tree, the displayed table and the complete unfiltered breakdown can each be downloaded.

task.text: Show how well each part of a taxonomic clade is covered by each kind of public genomic data, so gaps and well-sampled groups can be found before planning a study.

data.text: A taxonomy tree whose species carry counts of four kinds of public resources, rolled up into coverage and totals for every clade at every rank.
data.item: a clade at the chosen rank, with its species count and, per resource, the species covered, the percent covered and the total count

stage.text: surveying what public genomic data exists across a clade, before designing a comparative study

mechanism.text: A root clade chosen in the sidebar drives summary cards for the whole clade; a rank control and a gated form of filter, sort and limit settings then produce one result set that is drawn both as a tree with per-group diverging bar charts and as a sortable table, in tabs. A separate export section writes the full unfiltered breakdown with a preview.

field.text: surveying sequencing-data availability across a taxonomy in comparative genomics

workflow.name: break a hierarchy into groups and tally how many members of each have each kind of resource

steps.step: choose the part of the hierarchy to work on
steps.here: pick a common clade from the sidebar list or type any NCBI taxon ID; a lineage breadcrumb shows where it sits

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: total species plus one card per resource with species covered, a percent-covered bar, the total count and a link out to the source database

steps.step: split the collection into groups at a chosen level
steps.here: a segmented control lists only ranks below the root's own; an explainer reports how many groups that rank yields

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: require one or more resources with ALL/ANY logic, drop groups with no data, sort by species or any coverage or total, and cap the number shown, then press Generate Tree & Table
the same groups shown as a tree with diverging bars per leaf (assemblies and annotations one side, RNA-Seq the other) and as a table with coverage progress bars that re-sorts by column
download the tree as SVG, the displayed rows as TSV, or the complete never-filtered breakdown as TSV after a ten-row preview

distinctive: coverage is counted twice per resource: the number of species that have at least one, and the total number of records, so breadth and depth are separate
the valid breakdown levels depend on the chosen root's own rank in the taxonomy
the displayed set is capped by a hard limit for rendering, while a separate export always holds every group unfiltered
counts are precomputed weekly from several public archives and rolled up through the taxonomy to every clade
